# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — single-file `package.json` metadata. No version, dependency, script, or release surface moves; `+1/-27` is one description line and 26 keywords.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** This is the remove half of the custody split whose receive half I approved as Brain #183, so I reviewed it as a **pair** rather than in isolation, and computed the sets rather than reading the body's classification. The result is exact on every axis: Engine **66 → 40**, and the 26 removed terms are **precisely** the Brain-only set #183 received — not a near-match, an identity. All 9 shared terms are retained here, and after both halves land the Engine∩Brain overlap is **exactly those 9** (`neo-mjs`, `software-organism`, `self-evolving`, `self-healing-software-organism`, `neural-link`, `possession-interface`, `conversational-application-embodiment`, `live-application-mutability`, `ai-native`) — the intentional bridge set and nothing else. `40 = 31 Engine + 9 shared`; the body's "Dropped: none" holds mechanically. The thing I went looking for and did not find: a term lost between the two halves. There is none — every one of the original 66 is now accounted for in exactly one or both packages by design.

**Findings:** None. One tension worth recording so nobody re-litigates it.

**The description reframing looks like §neo_identity_anchor drift and is not.** The lead moves from *"a self-evolving software organism: a professional end-to-end AI engineering team…"* to *"a multi-threaded application engine — the Body of a self-evolving software organism — …"*, and `neo.mjs` is the org's **published** package, so this is the single most-read identity surface we have. My reflex was that leading with the Engine confirms exactly the pre-training prior the anchor exists to nullify.

[#17807](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17807) answers it, and the answer is right: *"Framing is audience-segmented: the README may lead with the whole organism, while the npm package description must make the Engine product legible."* The anchor forbids reducing **Neo-as-whole** to the Body — and post-split the npm package `neo.mjs` **is** the Body; the Brain is a separate package. Describing the artifact accurately is not category drift. The retained appositive *"the Body of a self-evolving software organism"* keeps the parent relationship discoverable, which satisfies the Contract Ledger's "compatible with the organism apex". Fix item 1 prescribes this wording almost verbatim, so it is authorized rather than invented.

I am recording this because a reviewer arriving with the anchor loaded will have my reaction, and the ticket's resolution is one level deeper than the anchor's text.
